title: Roos completeness, actual open completion units and the complete adjunction
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $e:V\hookrightarrow W$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Put $C_W(H)=R\lim Q_W(H)_\bullet$ and let $\eta_H:H\to C_W(H)$ be the actual strict quotient-augmentation map. Define $C_V$ likewise. Then $V,W$ are Noetherian and qcqs, $e$ is quasi-compact, and $(R,(t))$ satisfies the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $R$ is Noetherian, $A_1$ is additive torsion, every $A_n$ is finite and has the finite free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$. The open coefficient identifications $e^{-1}(A_n)_W=(A_n)_V$ and $e^{-1}B_W=B_V$ preserve constant sections and every quotient projection.
For every $H$, $C_W(H)$ is intrinsically derived $(t)$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and for every intrinsically complete $L$, precomposition with $\eta_H$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(C_W(H),L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,L)$. The Roos-triangle completeness predicate [def-weil-derived-complete] holds for $H$ if and only if $\eta_H$ is invertible, equivalently if and only if $H$ is intrinsically complete; the same assertions hold on $V$.
There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\rho_H:e^*C_W(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_V(e^*H)$, induced by the coefficient-compatible reduction-tower comparison and the normalized exact-product Roos comparison, satisfying $\rho_H\circ e^*\eta_H=\eta_{e^*H}$. Restriction preserves completeness and its comparison to completed open pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is this actual completion unit, hence is invertible on complete objects. Extension $e_!$ preserves completeness. The open adjunction restricts to the full complete subcategories, its unit $M\to e^*e_!M$ is the identity under the section-normalized slice identification, and $e_!$ on these subcategories is fully faithful.

proof.text: Prove the coefficient datum from extension_integers_dvr, finiteness of the recorded quotient rings, and standard_quotients_perfect. The nonzero maximal-ideal generator gives injectivity of uniformizer powers; Ideal.mem_span_singleton and the quotient API give exactness and surjectivity.
Mathlib finite-type and Noetherian instances give Noetherianness, compactness, quasi-separatedness, and quasi-compactness of the open immersion.

Apply integralRoosReflector on W and V. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative and apply the existing five-way Roos/intrinsic equivalence, conditions 0 and 4, to prove IsComplete iff the actual unit is invertible. Assemble the four reflector assertions.

Obtain coefficient Operations from openRoosCoefficientOperations. Prove finiteMap invertibility directly: the normalized map equals the composite of the two pullback-sheafification compatibility isomorphisms, since they agree on constants. Prove every quotient-transition square by applying systemMap naturality to a horizontal arrow of the coefficient sequence site. These give a natural isomorphism of the finite section diagrams. Both completed coefficient section cones are limiting; projections identifies the completed map with a cone morphism between the transported limit cones, so it is invertible.

Apply openRoosFunctorTransport for rho, the strict pulled Roos comparison c, and sigma. Their unit equations and the actual-unit completeness criterion prove preservation of completeness by restriction and extension. Set C=completion_W followed by star, chi=star applied to eta_W, and b=rho to obtain the requested pulled comparison.
For another unit-compatible rho, use the reflector Hom bijection into completion_V(star(H)) to show equality objectwise, canceling the chosen rho inverse. Thus the comparison is unique.

Prove the ordinary localized extension unit invertible by the subterminality of the open object: its direct-sum extension has one summand on the open. Use the normalized sheafification unit equation, then compose with the coefficient equivalence. Derive invertibility for complexes termwise and for all derived objects by essential surjectivity of Q and the localization unit formula. Restrict the original derived adjunction to the full complete subcategories using restrictFullyFaithful; its unit and counit map to the specified ones. The restricted unit is invertible, so the left adjoint is fully faithful.
